questions.stem: Which is the correct order of the critical rendering path?
choices: Parse HTML + CSS → Render tree → Layout → Paint → Composite
questions.explanation: DOM + CSSOM combine into the render tree, then layout computes geometry, paint fills pixels, and composite stitches layers.

questions.stem: Which CSS change is a composite-only operation (no layout, no paint)?
questions.explanation: transform (and opacity) on a layer-promoted element runs on the GPU, skipping layout and paint.

questions.stem: What does `<script async>` do?
choices: Downloads in parallel and runs as soon as ready, possibly before the DOM is parsed
questions.explanation: async fetches in parallel and executes immediately on availability, which means order is not guaranteed and parsing may pause.

questions.stem: What does `<script defer>` guarantee?
choices: Runs in document order, after HTML parsing finishes but before DOMContentLoaded
Runs before the DOM is parsed
questions.explanation: defer scripts download in parallel, run after parsing in document order, then DOMContentLoaded fires.

questions.stem: Which call forces a synchronous layout (reflow)?
questions.explanation: Reading offsetHeight/Width/Top, getBoundingClientRect, etc forces the browser to flush any pending style/layout work.
Sync first (1, 4). Microtasks drain before macrotasks, so 3 (Promise) before 2 (setTimeout).

questions.stem: Layout thrashing happens when:
choices: Too many CSS files are loaded
Code interleaves reads (offsetWidth) and writes (style changes) in a loop, forcing repeated layout
questions.explanation: Each read after a write invalidates and re-runs layout. Batch all reads first, then all writes.

questions.stem: Which CSS change triggers a repaint but not a reflow?
questions.explanation: Colour changes don't affect box geometry, so layout is skipped. Anything that changes size/position triggers reflow.

questions.stem: Cache-Control: max-age=31536000, immutable is appropriate for:
questions.explanation: Fingerprinted assets never change at the same URL, so they can be cached for a year and skip revalidation.

questions.stem: Which metric measures responsiveness to user interactions?
questions.explanation: INP (Interaction to Next Paint) replaced FID as the Core Web Vital for responsiveness. Target < 200ms.

questions.stem: What does `display: none` vs `visibility: hidden` mean for the render tree?
choices: Both remove the element from the render tree
display:none removes it from the render tree; visibility:hidden keeps the box but makes it invisible
visibility:hidden removes it; display:none reserves space
questions.explanation: display:none means no box at all (no space reserved). visibility:hidden keeps geometry; the element still takes layout space.

questions.stem: Why is JavaScript described as single-threaded with an event loop?
choices: One call stack runs at a time; async work returns control to the loop which dispatches queued callbacks
questions.explanation: The main thread runs to completion on each task, then drains microtasks, then renders, then picks the next task. No true concurrency on the main thread.

questions.stem: Which header lets the server return 304 Not Modified for unchanged resources?
questions.explanation: Client sends If-None-Match with the previously received ETag. If unchanged, the server returns 304 with no body.

questions.stem: A `<script>` tag without async/defer is encountered during parsing. What happens?
choices: Parser pauses, fetches and executes the script, then resumes
questions.explanation: Classic scripts are parser-blocking. The HTML parser stops until the script is downloaded and executed.

questions.stem: Animating `left` from 0 to 300px will:
choices: Run on the GPU with no layout
questions.explanation: left changes box position, which triggers layout. Use transform: translateX for composited animations.

questions.stem: Which is true about microtasks vs macrotasks?
choices: The microtask queue is fully drained between each macrotask
questions.explanation: After each task, the loop drains the entire microtask queue before potentially rendering and picking the next task.

questions.stem: What does CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) penalise?
choices: Visible content jumping around as the page loads
questions.explanation: CLS measures the total amount of unexpected layout shift during load. Reserve space for images/ads to avoid penalties.

questions.stem: requestAnimationFrame runs callbacks:
choices: Before the next paint, synchronized to the display refresh
questions.explanation: rAF is the right hook for visual updates — it batches with the compositor and avoids extra reflows.

questions.stem: A long synchronous JS task blocks:
choices: Rendering, user input handling, and timers — everything on the main thread
questions.explanation: The main thread is shared between JS, layout, paint, and event delivery. A long task starves all of them.

questions.stem: Why use Web Workers?
choices: To access the DOM in a separate thread
To run CPU-heavy work off the main thread without blocking UI
questions.explanation: Workers give you a real OS thread for computation. They communicate via postMessage and cannot touch the DOM.

questions.stem: What does `Cache-Control: no-store` mean?
questions.explanation: no-store forbids any cache (browser, proxy) from storing the response. Use for authenticated/sensitive responses.

questions.stem: Which step is skipped for a transform-only animation on a promoted layer?
questions.explanation: If the element is already on a separate compositor layer, the GPU handles the transform without layout or repaint.

questions.stem: DOMContentLoaded fires when:
choices: All images and stylesheets are loaded
The initial HTML has been parsed and deferred scripts have run, but external subresources may still be loading
questions.explanation: DOMContentLoaded marks the DOM being ready. The `load` event fires later, after images/stylesheets/etc finish.

questions.stem: Why does inlining critical CSS in <head> improve LCP?
choices: It avoids a render-blocking round trip for above-the-fold styling
questions.explanation: External stylesheets block render. Inlining the minimum CSS needed for the first paint lets the browser draw without waiting.

questions.stem: Which is the LCP target for a 'good' rating?
questions.explanation: Web Vitals: LCP < 2.5s good, 2.5-4s needs improvement, > 4s poor.
